package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code attempts to access sensitive credential files and exfiltrates their contents to an external server during package installation, which is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts should only handle package installation logic and should not access or transmit user credential files or perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup or migration, but they do not transmit sensitive data to external servers, especially during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to send data to app.threatest.com
Exfiltration of file contents during installation phase

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read and exfiltrated to an external server controlled by the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config during package installation
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com from setup.py or during pip install
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing hardcoded references to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI packages whose setup.py scripts access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and initiate outbound network connections, especially to app.threatest.com. Automated static analysis should flag any setup.py containing both file read operations on credential files and network exfiltration code. Network monitoring should alert on POST requests to app.threatest.com originating from Python installation processes.
